title: With great love
hook: the second blessing: with great love you have loved us; help us understand

segments.voice: Yesterday, reshut: the angels who give each other permission before they praise. Your line was they give each other leave. Today, the second blessing before the Shema.

Kids learn from people who love them. A child will sit still for a grandmother's story far longer than for a stranger's lecture. Students try harder for the coach who believes in them. Love comes first, and learning grows in it. Soon the morning service reaches the Shema, with its command: you shall love the LORD your God. But right before it comes a blessing that says, in effect: before you're asked to love, hear how much you're loved.
screen: `KIDS LEARN FROM PEOPLE WHO LOVE THEM.` → `LOVE FIRST, THEN LEARNING.` → `BEFORE YOU'RE ASKED TO LOVE.`

segments.voice: The blessing begins ahavah rabbah ahavtanu: with great love you have loved us. With great and overflowing compassion you have had compassion on us. Then it turns to learning. Our father, our king, for the sake of our ancestors who trusted you, and whom you taught the laws of life, teach us too. Then a chain of verbs: put it in our hearts to understand and to discern, to listen, to learn and to teach, to keep, to do and to fulfill. Eight steps, from first understanding all the way to living it. Light up our eyes with your Torah. Let our hearts hold on to your commandments. Unite our hearts to love and revere your name. It closes: blessed are you, who chooses his people Israel in love. Now the order. The very next thing said is the Shema, with its line from Deuteronomy, in the old Jewish translation: "And thou shalt love the LORD thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might." The command to love comes right after a blessing about being loved. The Talmud, in tractate Berakhot, records two opinions on how this blessing should open: with great love, or with everlasting love, and leaves both standing. Later custom kept both. In the Ashkenazi rite, great love opens the morning blessing and everlasting love the evening one; in many Sephardi communities, everlasting love is said at both.
screen: `WITH GREAT LOVE YOU HAVE LOVED US.` · `TEACH US, AS YOU TAUGHT THEM.` · `UNDERSTAND, LEARN, TEACH, DO.` · `LOVED, THEN ASKED TO LOVE.` · then, large: `GREAT LOVE FIRST.`

segments.voice: Remember one person who loved you while you were learning something hard, and stay with that for a moment. From there, name one thing you don't understand yet, a person, a text, a part of yourself, simply and honestly. If you pray, you can ask in the blessing's own words: put it in our hearts to understand.
Ahavah Rabbah. Great love: the blessing before the morning Shema that speaks of being loved before being asked to love.
Your line: great love first. Loved, and then asked to love. Day five hundred sixty-four, done.

howItsDone: Ahavah Rabbah is the second blessing before the Shema in the Ashkenazi morning service, said just before the Shema itself; many Sephardi communities say Ahavat Olam, everlasting love, in its place.
